newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian sees no problems with creditors.
newsitem.headline: Canadian sees no problems with creditors.

text.p: Canadian Airlines Corp executives said on Wednesday the company's creditors were generally supportive of its financial restructuring package, which included delayed payments on debt and aircraft leases.
Canadian chief financial officer Doug Carty told a conference call that Canadian officials heard no problems "of substance" among the 70 creditors at meetings in the past three months.
Carty said that no deadline had been set for the group to sign on to the plan, although the company hoped for agreement by mid-year.
Canadian chief executive Kevin Benson said that all the company's aircraft were in operation and no company had threatened to repossess any equipment.
Canadian, citing consumer doubt over its financial health, high fuel costs and poor weather in December, said earlier today its 1996 loss deepened to C$138.1 million from C$129.4 million in 1995.
Benson said it was too early in the company's 48-month restructuring plan to determine its ultimate success, but he said the early signs were positive.
All parts of Canadian's plan of cost cutting, route restructuring, wage cuts and tax breaks must be in place to garner full creditor support.
The Canadian government has yet to sign on with the fuel tax rebates to which Transport Minister David Anderson agreed in December.
Media reports over the past two days suggested that a conflict between Anderson and Finance Minster Paul Martin over the rebates was delaying the process.
But Benson said he hoped that with Canada's federal budget now out of the way, Ottawa would agree officially to the program within the next two weeks.
Benson said strong traffic figures in January resulted in a stronger than expected cash position for Canadian.
The carrier said on Wednesday that it had cash reserves of C$68.4 million at December 31, compared to C$200 million at the end of 1995.
